items.title: UoH-led team develops new alloy for safer medical implants
points: Researchers from the University of Hyderabad (UoH) here, in collaboration with IIT-Delhi, IIT-Bhubaneswar and CSIR-CECRI, Karaikudi, have developed a new family of metal alloys that could lead to stronger, safer and longer-lasting medical implants.

Instead of starting with one base metal and adding small amounts of others, researchers developed multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) by blending titanium, cobalt, and chromium in equal proportions.
This alloy has demonstrated high strength, excellent wear and corrosion resistance, and improved flexibility closer to that of natural bone, researchers said.
The findings were published in international journal Advanced Healthcare Materials.
They added that laboratory tests confirmed the alloy’s biocompatibility, and cell studies showed healthy cell growth without toxic effects.
According to information by the university, the study forms part of the doctoral research of Nanda Kishore Karnam, under the supervision of Koteswararao V.
Rajulapati, professor in the School of Engineering Sciences and Technology.

items.title: Kerala Police introduce HM ACTS, HOMeS platforms to expedite grievance redressal and enhance crime monitoring
points: HM ACTS is designed to ensure the systematic registration, tracking and timely disposal of complaints and petitions submitted to the Home Minister and his office.

Under the system, petitions received by the Home Minister’s office will be digitally registered and forwarded to the respective police offices through the Kerala Police’s existing software infrastructure.
Depending on the nature of a petition, the Home Minister’s office can issue appropriate directions to the police office concerned.
The progress of each petition can subsequently be monitored, thereby enabling the Minister’s office to identify complaints that remain unresolved and initiate follow-up measures.

Mr. Chennithala pointed out that the initiative was intended to address the delays that often frustrate complainants, particularly those who approach the Home Minister’s office after failing to obtain a timely response from local police stations.
HOMeS is a real-time crime-monitoring and administrative dashboard intended for the Home Minister and senior officials of the Home department.

Uttarkashi District Disaster Management Officer (DDMO) Shardul Gusain said that a joint team comprising the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and the Nehru Institute of Mountaineering (NIM) located the bodies during a search operation near Kedar Kharak.

The rotation will provide additional connections between major Chinese export gateways and key African markets, supporting the movement of goods across established and emerging trade routes.

The China Africa Link is a tangible example of DP World Marine Services’ Connected Trade Corridors approach, bringing together maritime solutions, ports and inland transport to create more integrated and flexible trade networks.

By expanding shipping connections into key African gateways, the service will provide customers with additional routing options, support growing trade flows and strengthen links between regional and international markets.
The new China Africa Link demonstrates how we are bringing our Connected Trade Corridors approach to life.

items.title: Iron Ore Slips on Rising Shipments
points: Iron ore futures declined toward CNY 670 per ton, remaining close to four-year lows as increasing global supply continued to pressure the market.

Industry data showed that shipments from major producers Australia and Brazil climbed 1.3% week-on-week to 27.9 million tons as of November 2, with miners boosting output to meet their quarterly and annual production targets.

Meanwhile, demand in China, the world’s largest iron ore consumer, remained subdued as steelmakers held back on restocking amid persistently weak profit margins, softer downstream steel demand and elevated inventory levels.
Environmental restrictions imposed across several northern Chinese provinces also continued to constrain hot metal production.
However, output is expected to rebound once these restrictions are lifted.

items.title: Coal supply is struggling to keep pace with demand
points: Global coal supply is struggling to keep pace with rising Asian demand as production constraints and higher prices tighten the market, potentially pushing thermal coal prices higher this winter, according to Bank of America (BofA) analysts.
Benchmark Australian prices have surged 40% this year to around $150 per metric ton, their highest level in two years, supported by stronger consumption and limited seaborne supplies.
BofA expects prices to remain supported through winter as elevated natural gas costs encourage power producers to switch to coal, particularly across Asia.
The Middle East conflict has tightened liquefied natural gas supplies, pushing Asian above $30 per million British thermal units and European beyond €90 per megawatt-hour this month.
At current gas prices, BofA estimates Newcastle coal could reach more than $350 per ton before losing its cost advantage over natural gas, suggesting considerable room for coal prices to rise.
South Korea has led recent demand growth, alongside emerging Asian economies including Vietnam and Pakistan, where higher energy costs have strengthened coal’s appeal.

items.title: Steel Declines to Near Three-Month Low
points: Steel rebar futures fell toward CNY 3,000 per ton, hitting near three-month lows as weak profit margins, sluggish downstream demand and elevated inventory levels continued to pressure the market.
Environmental restrictions across several northern Chinese provinces also weighed on hot metal production, although output is expected to rebound once the restrictions are lifted.
Meanwhile, the World Steel Association recently downgraded its global steel demand outlook, projecting a 0.1% contraction this year, reversing its earlier forecast of 0.3% growth made in April.
According to the report, Chinese steel consumption is expected to fall by 2% this year as the property sector downturn proves more prolonged than previously anticipated.
In contrast, India remains the fastest-growing major steel market, with demand forecast to increase by 7.9% in 2026 and 8% in 2027.

items.title: Russia exploring possibility of Arctic gas work with US partners: Putin

items.title: TN unveils Battery Storage Policy to become country's premier green energy hub

Issued through an energy department notification, the newly enacted framework aims to transform the state into India's foremost storage hub by attracting large-scale private investments and modernising energy infrastructure.
The policy, which was released on Tuesday, sets an ambitious target to deploy at least 2.5 GW, matching a 10 GWh storage capacity across the state during its operative period.

Accordingly, operating under the nodal agency Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation Limited , the initiative aims to tackle the complexities of variable renewable generation, optimise grid operations, and significantly reduce power curtailment.

By storing surplus electricity during low-demand hours-specifically leveraging solar generation windows-and discharging power during peak demand periods, the policy addresses vital energy security requirements.

HT reported AP Singh highlighted the station’s multifaceted role, including the administrative support it provides to Air Headquarters and more than 5,000 personnel.
Its abrupt closure forced the cancellation of Singh’s farewell golf event, scheduled for October 28, raising questions over the timing of the move.

items.title: ₹438 crore mephedrone seizure case: Gujarat ATS arrests international drug trafficker Salim Dola
points: Ahmedabad, The Gujarat ATS has arrested international drug trafficker Salim Ismail Dola, deported from Turkiye earlier this year, in connection with the seizure of mephedrone valued at ₹438.64 crore from a Vadodara factory in 2022, officials said on Tuesday.
In April this year, the Narcotics Control Bureau brought Dola back from Turkiye, where he was arrested on the basis of an Interpol Red Notice issued at India's request in March 2024.
The Gujarat Anti-Terrorist Squad took Dola into custody on October 31, Assistant Commissioner of Police, ATS, SL Chaudhary said.
The ATS had raided a drug manufacturing unit near Sindhrot village in Vadodara district on December 1, 2022, and seized 87.728 kg of mephedrone , valued at ₹438.64 crore in the international market.
A total of 10 accused have been arrested in the case, registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act.

items.title: Air India to shift more West-bound capacity from Delhi to Mumbai amid Pakistan airspace closure
points: Air India will shift more of its Europe- and US-bound capacity to Mumbai from Delhi as the continued closure of Pakistani airspace hits its western-bound network harder from the national Capital, the airline’s chief executive officer (CEO) Tewolde…
“Most of our network, unfortunately, in Europe and America, has been affected by the airspace closure,” Gebremariam said at the Aviation India and South Asia 2026 conference in New Delhi.
Gebremariam said the airline would continue operating flights to Europe and the US from the Capital, but move a larger share of the capacity to Mumbai.
He said the airline is exploring Bengaluru as a third hub in addition to Delhi and Mumbai, as it looks to build its international connectivity.
The airline is looking to improve efficiencies by bringing its full-service and low-cost operations, Air India and Air India Express, closer together in areas such as common corporate functions.

items.title: National Conference MP Aga Ruhullah resigns from Srinagar Lok Sabha seat
points: Srinagar MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi on Tuesday resigned from his parliamentary seat and also quit the ruling Jammu and Kashmir National Conference (NC) during a public gathering in Budgam.
The announcement came on the 26th anniversary of his father's death, as a large number of supporters had gathered at Behesht-e-Zehra Park in Budgam for the event.
Ruhullah Mehdi had actively campaigned for the NC during the 2024 Assembly elections.
However, he was also the first to publicly challenge his own government, accusing it of failing to fulfil poll promises on reservations, Article 370 and statehood.
In response, NC leaders challenged the Srinagar MP to resign from his Lok Sabha seat, arguing that the seat belonged to the party.
Notably, the high-profile seat had been vacated by Omar Abdullah after he retained the Ganderbal constituency following his victory from both seats in 2024.
In 2024, he contested the Lok Sabha election from the Srinagar constituency and won by a comfortable margin.

items.title: CM Naidu thanks Centre for support as Cyclone Murasu disrupts life in Andhra
points: Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Tuesday thanked the Centre for its "prompt support and solidarity" during severe cyclonic storm Murasu, which has damaged standing crops across thousands of acres in 15 districts and disrupted…
Naidu said the state machinery was working in close coordination with Central teams to carry out rescue and relief operations and clear roads.
"Dear Amit Shah ji, my heartfelt thanks for the Centre's prompt support and solidarity during cyclone Murasu.
Earlier, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said he had spoken to Naidu over the phone and taken stock of the impact of Cyclone Murasu.
He said he had assured Naidu that the Centre would extend all possible assistance and support.
National Disaster Response Force and State Disaster Response Force teams were already on the ground, undertaking relief operations and assisting people in the cyclone-affected areas, he said.
The Government of India stood with the people of Andhra Pradesh and was prepared to respond to any situation, Shah added.

items.title: Oppo Find X10 Pro Max Review: A Photography Monster With One Catch
points: The Oppo Find X10 Pro Max is an ambitious flagship with one of the most versatile camera systems available in the Indian market.
It packs three 200-megapixel rear cameras, which are not merely about resolution; they consistently produce pleasing photographs across landscapes, zoom shots, and challenging lighting.
The 6.78-inch LTPO AMOLED display is among the finest we have seen on an Oppo phone, while the Dimensity 9600 Pro keeps the experience fast and responsive.
Battery life is another major strength, with the 8,000mAh battery pack comfortably lasting beyond a day of use.
However, video recording is less dependable than the still-camera experience, and Oppo's AI features don't quite match its flagship ambitions.
At Rs 1,99,999, the asking price is the biggest obstacle to recommending an otherwise excellent smartphone.

items.title: Bhutan's glacial lake outburst exposes growing disaster threat across the Himalayas
points: Bhutan experienced a significant glacial lake outburst that raised concerns regarding devastating glacial floods in the Himalayas.

India, sharing river systems with Bhutan, has started its own review of disaster preparedness plans.
